law_name: 13th AHV/AVS pension (popular initiative "For a better life in old age")
description: Popular initiative for a 13th annual AHV/AVS old-age pension payment, accepted by 58.2% of voters on 3 March 2024. As Home Affairs minister, Baume-Schneider defended the Federal Council's recommendation to reject the initiative, then led its implementation, including the politically contested question of financing (e.g. via VAT and/or wage contributions).
significance: First successful expansion of AHV/AVS benefits via popular initiative; required Baume-Schneider's department to design financing and implementation against her own party's campaign position.

law_name: Premium relief initiative ("Maximum 10% du revenu pour les primes d'assurance-maladie")
description: SP/PS popular initiative to cap health-insurance premiums at 10% of disposable income, rejected by 55.5% of voters on 9 June 2024. Baume-Schneider defended the Federal Council and Parliament's counter-project and recommendation to reject.
significance: Major federal vote on health-insurance affordability; defeat for her own party's flagship initiative while she defended the government line as Health minister.

law_name: Cost-brake initiative (initiative pour un frein aux coûts de la santé)
description: Le Centre's popular initiative for a brake on health-care costs, rejected by voters on 9 June 2024. The Federal Council's counter-project foresees four-yearly cost-control objectives in mandatory health insurance, with first objectives from 2026.
significance: Part of the same June 2024 health-policy vote; Baume-Schneider defended the government counter-project and signalled continued action on costs and premiums.

law_name: EFAS — Uniform financing of health-care services (amendment to the Health Insurance Act)
description: Reform establishing uniform financing of outpatient and inpatient care (and later long-term care) by insurers and cantons, approved by 53.3% of voters on 24 November 2024 after a referendum led by the VPOD/SSP union ("Stop EFAS"). Baume-Schneider championed the reform as Health minister.
significance: Largest structural reform of Swiss health-care financing in decades; a notable ballot-box success for Baume-Schneider, especially coming after the rejected pension reform.

description: Reform of the second-pillar occupational pension system (BVG/LPP), rejected by voters (about 67% no) on 22 September 2024. Baume-Schneider, as Home Affairs minister, defended the reform supported by the Federal Council and Parliament.
significance: Clear defeat of the government-backed pension reform; a significant setback for her department in 2024.

law_name: Asylum practice for Afghan women and girls (SEM/FDJP)
description: From July 2023, under Baume-Schneider's FDJP, the State Secretariat for Migration adopted a practice allowing Afghan women and girls to obtain refugee status given the systematic persecution of women under the Taliban. The measure drew strong criticism from the SVP/UDC and parts of the PLR/FDP.
significance: Notable asylum-policy decision during her year at Justice and Police; central to right-wing criticism of her migration record.
